result.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations
result.summary: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of the continuation monad proposed to address the inefficiencies associated with the selection monad in alpha-beta search. We illustrate our approach with an implementation of Tic-Tac-Toe, observing a 39-fold reduction in the number of plays evaluated, compared with exhaustive search, in computing an optimal play. Finally, we formally establish the correctness of our construction by proving that the monadic alpha-beta search computes the same optimal outcomes and plays as exhaustive minimax search. Our results demonstrate how a foundational algorithm in AI can be expressed and verified using standard monadic abstractions, providing a basis for further development of compositional approaches to adversarial search.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用 continuation monad 与 reader monad 的组合形式化 alpha-beta 剪枝，把搜索界记录在 monadic 结果而非走法类型中，并说明普通 continuation monad 即可同时算出最优结果与最优走法序列；作者在井字棋上实现（相较穷举搜索评估走法数减少 39 倍），并证明其结果与穷举 minimax 一致。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「哪些分支可安全跳过」的可证明剪枝构造，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛除、搜索宽度控制与提前停止决策提供可供核查的抽象框架，但论文完全不涉及视觉或多模态内部状态，迁移需较多工作。
